Perhaps if Liverpool were playing a team with a bit more savvy, the 2-0 scoreline they currently protect would have been in jeopardy. Ipswich have put some nice moves together and had half chances but not enough to really turn the screw. Andoni Iraola, certainly, has been unhappy at times and it is becoming a trademark to see him spin around from the technical area in disgust when a ball has been squandered. In the main, though, he can be satisfied with this opening 45 minutes. Liverpool should be winning from here.

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Wirtz feeds a lovely pass into the left channel to pick out the run of Isak into the Ipswich box but Diop comes in with a crucial challenge.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Araujo slices a clearance out of play for an Ipswich corner. A real gift for the home side as Araujo was not under any real pressure.

Isak should head away at the near post but it comes to Mac Allister to clear away.

A chance for Wirtz as the ball falls to the German on the edge of the Ipswich box but his shot is saved by Scherpen down to his left.

Enciso is the first Ipswich player into the book tonight for delaying a restart.

Szoboszlai, for the third time in the half, shoots from range. Again, the Hungarian gets plenty of power on it but fortunately for Scherpen it is straight at him.

Enciso turns neatly not far outside the Liverpool box and then shoots but slices the shot a fair way wide.

Tommy Elphick, a member of Andoni Iraola’s coaching staff, is booked for his protestations. Liverpool are not happy with some of the fouls being given against them and then some that are not given for them, including a clear foul from Emersonn on Van Dijk that was not penalised.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

Mac Allister receives a pass from Wirtz and, from just outside the box, decides to shoot but his effort goes just over. Scherpen did appear to have it covered anyway.

A crucial intervention from Araujo. Enciso drives down Ipswich’s right after Fatawu’s header, with Mac Allister tracking back. From the right side of the Liverpool box, Enciso’s deflected cross comes towards Maeda at the far post but Araujo makes an important clearance.

Moments later, Davis again meets a Fatawu cross at the far post but his header is off target.

Fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right all the way to the back post finds Davis, who heads back across goal. Emersonn takes a touch with his chest on the edge of the six-yard box before shooting but Jacquet is on hand to make a crucial block. Ipswich though do have their first corner of the game.

Lukic clips it in and Alisson should punch away with ease. However, the ball comes off Gakpo and, very fortunately for Alisson, the ball gets trapped between his own legs and he can gather. Alisson will be a relieved man.

Szoboszlai sends another powerful shot from range towards the goal and forces Scherpen into another decent save. Ipswich are not helping themselves at times by just giving the ball away inside their own half.

Szoboszlai comes close to adding a third for Liverpool. Fatawu inexplicably gives the ball away inside his own half before Mac Allister plays it forward to Szoboszlai, who takes just one touch before firing towards goal. Scherpen gets down well to his right to make the save.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Mac Allister, who is booked slightly harshly for a foul on Enciso.

Moments later, Ipswich have their first effort of the game but Fatawu curls over from the edge of the box.

Another fine goal from Isak and Liverpool lead 2-0 not even 10 minutes into this game. It is Gakpo who assists again with a superb pass with the outside of his right foot from halfway into the left channel to pick out the run in behind of Isak. The Swede cuts inside Greaves onto his right before then chopping back onto his left. He then coolly slots home past Scherpen and Liverpool have the dream start.

Liverpool take a deserved lead at Portman Road. Kerkez wins the ball back for Liverpool on halfway and the ball comes to Gakpo. The Dutchman drives forward and spots Isak in space to his right. Isak’s movement is very clever as he drifts off the defender into space. He takes a touch before smashing the ball past Scherpen at his near post. Should Scherpen have saved that? Possibly but Isak did hit that very hard. For the first time this season, Liverpool lead in a Premier League match.

Fatawu swings it in with his left but Alisson punches away.

It has been all Liverpool in these early stages but have yet to have a shot. Ipswich have barely touched the ball thus far.

Liverpool win the first corner of the game as Davis is forced to put it behind after good work from Munoz down Liverpool’s right.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger is headed away from danger.

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

#1899. Antonio Conte sends message to Man Utd after missing out on Mauricio Pochettino’s job

Antonio Conte has played down suggestions he missed out on the Manchester United job because of his demanding reputation in management.

United made their third mid-season managerial change in three years after sacking Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino coming in as his replacement earlier this month.

Conte was among the names initially explored along with Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann. The Italian, a free agent since parting ways with Napoli, was thought to be keen on the role at Old Trafford but it was widely reported United had reservations over some of his methods.

The Italian led Juventus, Chelsea, Inter Milan and Napoli to league titles but has not lasted longer than two seasons at any club since leaving the Bianconeri in 2014.

Conte has a reputation for being hugely demanding with players and the board but in an interview with Cronache di Spogliatoio he insisted anyone scared of his approach is scared of winning.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The coach recalled a meeting with Sir Alex Ferguson during his time in charge of Chelsea, praising the standards the Scot said before insisting the idea United no longer want to meet those standards is ‘offensive’

‘If someone is scared of my method, then they’re scared of winning, because that methodology leads to winning,’ Conte said.

‘That’s my answer. United has such an important history that it seems strange to imagine anyone being scared of a job aimed at restoring the club to its former glory.

They last won the championship in 2013, under Ferguson. I have enormous respect for Sir Alex Ferguson. I’ve read his book, and when I was in London, I was lucky enough to go to his house and spend a day with him. He’s incredibly eager to talk about football, even if it’s sometimes hard to understand his Scottish accent.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘With his method and his approach, he made Manchester United great. That’s why I find certain words about United almost offensive: it’s like vetoing a return to their own history. The method is needed to achieve important results.

‘If you then tell me that it’s a method that needs work, I’d say yes: everyone needs to work, not just the players.’

#1898. Nations League draw in full as England, Wales, Republic of Ireland learn fates

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 11:28, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 11:47

England will play Norway in the quarter-finals of the UEFA Nations League.

The Three Lions progressed to the last eight as League A Group 3 winners, having collected 15 points from six matches, including a sensational 3-2 win over Spain on the final matchday.

England's first-placed status meant that they entered the draw as one of the four seeded quarter-finalists, alongside France, Germany and Portugal, while they were unable to be drawn against Spain having already faced them in the group stage.

Thomas Tuchel's side will therefore do battle with Erling Haaland's Norway, who finished as runners-up to Portugal in League A Group 4 and will be seeking revenge for their World Cup 2026 quarter-final defeat to England.

Should England prevail in their reunion with the Scandinavians, they will clash with either Belgium or Germany in the semi-finals, for the right to contest a heavyweight showpiece event.

?????????? Thomas Tuchel's #ThreeLions will face Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in March! https://t.co/TQBDCd9I4i

The headline quarter-final sees reigning world and European champions Spain square off with France, a repeat of the 2020-21 Nations League final which Les Bleus won 2-1.

Whoever wins that clash of the titans will pit their wits against either the Netherlands or Portugal, who also squared off in the final of the inaugural Nations League in 2019; the Selecao triumphed 1-0 thanks to a Goncalo Guedes strike.

The first legs of the Nations League quarter-finals will take place between March 25 and March 27, before the return fixtures are held across March 28 and March 30.

England will travel to Norway for their first clash, before welcoming the Nordic nation to Wembley for the return fixture. The semi-finals and final will then be held in June in an as yet undetermined host nation.

Meanwhile, the Republic of Ireland will take on Croatia in the League A/League B playoffs for the right to earn promotion to the top tier, while Wales must beat Slovenia to retain their League A status.

Wales finished bottom of League A Group 4 on three points, but survived automatic relegation to the second division thanks to their superior points total to Turkey and the Czech Republic (both 0).

The Dragons have only ever faced Slovenia once before, drawing 0-0 in a 2005 international friendly.

Ireland's runners-up finish in League B Group 3 means that they have the chance to rise to League A for the first time ever, having only competed in League B since the Nations League's inception.

The Boys in Green have only beaten Croatia twice in their previous seven meetings, though, and lost 3-1 during their most recent head-to-head at Euro 2012.

#1897. Harry Kane injury: Bayern Munich and England striker facing ‘months’ out

Harry Kane is facing several months out after suffering an ankle ligament injury during Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga game on Friday night.

The England captain was forced off after just 20 minutes following a challenge from defender Joel Schmied during Bayern’s 1-1 draw with FC Koln.

The 33-year-old, who won the Ballon d’Or last month, initially tried to carry on before he limped off the pitch alongside Bayern’s medical staff.

Bayern issued an update after the game which read: ‘Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against 1. FC Koln on Friday evening.

‘This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months.’

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Bayern have seven more fixtures until their winter break in December. The German champions resume their Bundesliga campaign on January 9 and are also due to play Manchester United in the Champions League on January 20.

‘We have to do it without Harry, we have to do it without these guys,’ said Bayern head coach Vincent Kompany.

‘They are world-class players. You can’t replace them. But we have the mentality and we have to bring that.’

Kane may also face a race to be fit for England’s Nations League quarter-final against Norway at the end of March.

#1896. Moretto: Milan among teams scouting ‘very promising’ Spain U19 international

AC Milan are monitoring Real Oviedo midfielder Enzo Perez closely, according to a report from Matteo Moretto.

Milan have shown a propensity in the past couple of years to go out and try procure young talent. Alphadjo Cisse and Sankhoun Diawara are examples of this in the first team, while it extends down to the Futuro and beyond.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Matteo Moretto spoke in a video on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel and he revealed that Milan have sent a scout to watch a midfielder in action in the second division in Spain.

“I want to talk about a young midfielder who plays for Oviedo. He’s a very promising young player. The information I have is that AC Milan have been to see him several times in recent weeks, or at least in the past few months. They even went to see him live recently,” he said (via MilanNews).

“Milan are one of the clubs closely monitoring the development of Enzo Perez, an 18-year-old midfielder for Oviedo. He has a release clause. He’s been playing consistently lately. I can say that there are other clubs besides AC Milan, including Espanyol, Betis and Brentford.

#1895. Lamine Yamal's sly jibe at Elliot Anderson: Unseen footage reveals the moment Spain star is caught calling rival 'stupid' as tempers flared in England's thrilling win over Spain

Published: 06:21 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 14:24 EST, 16 November 2026

Lamine Yamal mercilessly taunted England rival Elliot Anderson as tensions flared during the Three Lions’ spectacular victory over Spain on Sunday night.

England held on for a memorable 3-2 victory in Madrid after Anderson was given his marching orders with just under 30 minutes remaining.

Thomas Tuchel’s side were three goals in front and cruising when Anderson - looking to atone for a sloppy error from Jarrel Quansah - cynically hauled down 19-year-old Yamal as he barrelled down on goal.

Spain were awarded a penalty for the infringement, and Anderson was sent off - much to the Manchester City star’s bemusement.

But Yamal, aggrieved by Anderson’s challenge, made a beeline for the midfielder following the challenge. According to Spanish reports, the attacker mouthed ‘tonto, tonto’ to his rival following his dismissal.

The colloquial term can mean a number of things, varying from idiot, fool or stupid, but in any case is far from a term of affection.

🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨بطاقة حمراء لإليوت أندرسون ولامين يامال يستفزه🤯🤯#اسبانيا_انجلترا #دوري_الأمم_الأوروبية pic.twitter.com/cOrswp5kCC

Lamine Yamal was spotted taunting Elliot Anderson after the Manchester City midfielder was sent off for a challenge on the winger

The moment came in England's historic 3-2 win over the World Champions

Anderson blanked the 19-year-old while a VAR review confirmed the on-field official’s decision was the right one, eventually trudging off the pitch.

A fired-up Yamal galvanised the reigning world champions as they searched for an unlikely comeback.

Mikel Oyarzabal, the man who scored Spain’s winner against England two years ago in the 2024 Euros final, converted the spot kick before Nico Williams scored Spain’s second after latching on to an excellent Yamal cross.

However, Las Rojas fell short, with Sunday’s defeat their first in an imperious 43-game run.

A jubilant Thomas Tuchel hailed the match as his ‘best performance of my time as manager’.

‘What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,’ Tuchel said after the game. ’Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

‘It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.’

#1890. Hutchinson admits ‘dream’ is to be bought by Milan and insists Scudetto is possible

Omari Hutchinson has spoken about his preferred role, while praising the AC Milan fans and revealing his belief the Scudetto is a realistic target.

Hutchinson joined Milan on an initial loan deal from Nottingham Forest with an option to buy. He scored his first goal for the club in the away win over Udinese last month, and is getting more regular minutes on the right side.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In fact, the head coach Ruben Amorim has even deployed him as a wing-back on occasion. Given the injuries to Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze the Englishman’s role has become an even more important one than first imagined.

Hutchinson met with fans this afternoon at the Milan Store in San Babila in the city centre. While at the event, the winger gave an interview to the reporters who were present, with MilanNews relaying his words.

How have these first few months at Milan been? Are you raising your game?

“It’s going well, the coach is happy, but I think there’s still a lot to do. I’m earning myself some space… From here on out, we have to keep winning.”

We often see you on the wing. Do you prefer to play there or as a second striker?

“Personally, I like to play anywhere, but preferably on the right flank. Then, wherever the coach puts me, I try to adapt, do my job, and perform to my best, following his tactical instructions. He knows what I can do with the ball. He simply tells me to create and give my all.”

“He talks to me about what to do with the ball and to do my best.”

Why this difference in performance between Serie A and the Europa League?

“It’s hard to say… There have been games where we haven’t performed well due to silly mistakes, but I think we need to push forward from now on and get back on track for the Europa League. We have the right team to do it. We need to win and be at our best in every game.”

What has struck you most about the fans in Italy these past months?

“Definitely the passion surrounding the club. At the stadium, everyone is behind the team. It’s fantastic, I’ve never experienced anything like it before.”

“We’ve got the players, we have a good squad, and even though we’re still missing some leaders at times, I think we’re building on that. I think the coaches and the coaching staff are guiding us very well. Once everything clicks together perfectly, we’ll do great things.”

Do you still see yourself at Milan in the coming seasons?

“It’s my dream. After this season, I hope to be signed permanently. I see myself playing here for a long time to come.”

What’s the feeling of playing in a historic stadium like San Siro?

“It’s crazy. The fans, even the away fans… It’s a unique feeling. It makes you want to give your all for the fans, create special moments, and win.”

What are the differences between the Premier League and Serie A?

“They’re both tough. When other teams play against Milan, they always want to give their all. They’re always tough matches. Tactically, it’s more defensive here.

“In the Premier League, you probably have more space and the quality is probably a little higher, but Serie A is a tough league. There’s not that big a difference, there’s not that big a gap.”

Is there any team-mate you’ve grown close to?

“No, I have a good relationship with everyone. They’ve all welcomed me very well, and obviously it’s easier with the guys who speak English.”

Do you dream of making the national team?

“I’m trying to focus on my club. I want to perform well for Milan and then we’ll see.”

#1887. Under-17 World Cup: Five African wonderkids to watch, including Man United and Chelsea prospects

By Axel Clody | 20 Nov 2026 12:42

With ten representatives at The Under-17 World in Qatar, Africa has several promising generations, with players already noticed at the last Africa Cup of Nations and graduates of prestigious academies. Here are five profiles to watch closely, who could use this event to move up a level.

Some are already considered major figures in their national teams, while others will have the chance to make a name for themselves with the general public and recruiters.

Morocco have several interesting individuals, but Ibrahim Rabbaj is already considered the star of the team. Born in England, the 17-year-old forward plays for Chelsea, where he has gradually climbed the ranks until joining the Under-18 group. Creative, technical and able to play both centrally and on the flank, he has a fine attacking palette. Versatile, he has even occasionally filled in as a left-back at club level!

Already crowned African Under-17 champion with Morocco in 2025, he has been able to gauge the demands of major competitions. Under former international Ahmed Kantari, he will have the chance to confirm that his potential can also be expressed on the world stage.

Algeria return to the Under-17 World Cup for the first time since 2009 and will be able to count on Yacine Abed to lead their attack.

Trained at Paradou AC, the most prolific academy in the country, the forward particularly stood out at the last Under-17 Africa Cup of Nations, where he notably scored twice against South Africa (2-0), helping Algeria’s youngsters take a big step towards qualification.

Quick and technical, Abed has an interesting profile to unsettle opposing defences. This World Cup will be an opportunity to confirm his promise against opposition of a different calibre.

Interesting transfer as Ivorian youth international Harafat Diabaté (2009) ?? has committed to join Celta Vigo, officially signing next January. More on him soon! ? https://t.co/yyhc0ZdCsK

For Ivory Coast, Mohamed Harafat Diabate is a name to remember. The Celta Vigo forward, who joined in July from Racing Club d’Abidjan, could use this competition to make himself stand out. He had already caught the eye at the Under-17 Africa Cup of Nations, notably scoring the winning penalty against DR Congo (1-0) in the final minutes of the match.

Alongside players such as Hubert Yao Kouassi, he represents an additional option for an Ivorian side that is not short of ambition. His ability to be decisive in key moments will be watched particularly closely in Qatar.

Reigning African champions, Senegal have a particularly interesting generation. Among their talents, El Hadji Ibrahima Sow deserves particular attention. A product of AS Dakar Sacre-Coeur, which has produced Pathe Mboup, Alassane Ndao and Iliman Ndiaye, the attacking midfielder is already playing in the Senegalese top flight despite being 16.

His main quality is his vision of the game. Able to find spaces between the lines, deliver passes in the final metres and pose a threat from set pieces, Sow has the profile of a true playmaker. His intelligence and calm in decisive areas could help Senegal, who dream of taking another step after their continental triumph.

Finally, Cameroon will be able to count on Douka Nkoto, a midfielder in the Manchester United academy. Initially trained in Cameroon, at Player FC of Yaounde, he joined the Manchester United academy with his brother Bassirou. Although born in Cameroon, he had started out representing England before being brought back into the Cameroon fold through a step up to the Under-23 side, alongside his brother.

The two players, both born in 2010, are presented as modern midfielders, able to put in repeated efforts, win the ball back and push forward. Douka will notably need to show his ability to manage the rhythm and intensity of an international competition. For Cameroon, who have never yet got past the group stage of an Under-17 World Cup, his contribution in midfield could be valuable.

#1886. The boyish, Lego-obsessed son of a farmer who quit Man City to become England's No 1: How James Trafford - with £95m spent on him - is maturing to star for Leeds and the Three Lions

Published: 14:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 16:35 EST, 16 November 2026

'It was like meeting a kid at a sixth-form careers day'. That was the verdict, slightly unflattering but endearing all the same, of one Premier League chief after encountering James Trafford.

When, at England's World Cup base in Kansas City, I then sat down with Trafford and he revealed that his partner had packed some Lego for him to build in camp, you wondered if sixth-form was a grade too high.

He is the son of a Cumbrian farmer and the Lego was of a tractor, which he would save for later in the tournament. 'You don't want to go too early,' he said.

None of this is a criticism. Far from it. There was a boyish charm, an innocence, even, and Trafford was engaging company. Nonetheless, he did not sound ready for the likes of a World Cup semi-final against Argentina. Thomas Tuchel agreed.

But every boy will one day become a man. On a ferocious and febrile night in Madrid, no place for adolescents, we may just have witnessed James Trafford's graduation ceremony.

Without his double save in stoppage-time, England would have left Spain without a famous, and deserved, victory. One Spanish title labelled it 'la actuacion de su vida', the performance of his life. You wonder how much they saw of his loan spell at Accrington Stanley, but the sentiment stands.

James Trafford celebrates with Jarell Quansah, Dan Burn and Ezri Konsa during his starring performance in Spain

Trafford pictured with his farmer father, David, in the cab of his tractor with their dogs (Source: James Trafford)

Madrid daily AS exclaimed: 'Magisterio de Trafford!' Translated, 'A Trafford Masterclass!'. They claim he was the reason Spain could not complete their comeback, and they would be right.

When Tuchel stood with us in a corridor of the Metropolitano Stadium on the eve of the game, he had no issue confirming that Trafford would start. His message, though, was clear - it was sink or swim for a goalkeeper who turned 24 last month.

Not only did Trafford keep his head above water, it was he who pulled the team ashore. It was he to whom his senior colleagues ran in celebration. Ezri Konsa nearly took the shirt off Trafford's back, such was the force of his gratitude. But maybe this was the occasion when Trafford took the No 1 jersey from the back of Jordan Pickford, the holder for nearly a decade.

Pickford has done nothing wrong. Were Trafford to still display that maturity deficit, Pickford would be a reliable custodian heading to Euro 2028. This is not Peter Shilton post Italia 90, an uncomfortable truth of a great in need of the retirement barn. The 32-year-old has plenty to give on the back of all he has already given.

This, admitted Tuchel after the 3-2 win, is a selection dilemma that allows a manager to sleep well at night.

'There is no headache at all!' he boomed. 'I'm so far away from a headache, I cannot imagine.

Trafford left Manchester City with the plan to usurp Jordan Pickford as England No 1

Jude Bellingham certainly seemed impressed with the performance of the goalkeeper

'This is what we wanted. This is the best thing that can happen to all of us, also to Pickers. It is amazing how they push each other, and if then Traff has a performance like this, he has it because he knows he's well prepared. He gets the push from his colleagues and competitors.'

Tuchel has seen enough of Trafford in training and around camp to believe he is ready for promotion. He has watched him for Leeds, where he rates as the best performing goalkeeper in the Premier League. His 'net goals prevented' (4.4) and 'save percentage' (81.4) are higher than any rival this season, including Pickford.

'You always have to deserve your place,' added Tuchel. 'You will never get a gift and just get a game (for the sake of it). So he deserved to play and we expected this kind of performance. It was not only the last save, but also the build-up play and not losing focus. He has proved it on this stage, so this gives him a lot of belief. Now, it's on him to keep going for it.'

It, you presume, is the No 1 jersey. Trafford has made no secret of his desire to take it from Pickford, and he told us in the summer that such ambition was the motivation behind him wanting to leave Manchester City for a second time.

That day, he flipped his room key with a magician's sleight of hand throughout the interview, a dexterity useful for Lego. Better still for fingertip saves such as the one to deny Aymeric Laporte in the 91st minute.

Also in the gift pack from his girlfriend were two face masks. 'Very thoughtful,' he quipped. But that is another observation, bordering on concern, that some prospective buyers have made in recent years - on the goalkeeping scale of uber professional to joker, he resides too close to the latter. We have seen, even this season, the odd concentration lapse that speaks to that thought.

Trafford has played a starring role in goal since moving to Leeds United in the summer

But there was also a feeling that Trafford needed more exposure and responsibility before the penny dropped and his value was realised. Already, £95million has been spent on him in transfer fees.

At Leeds, and now with England, he has been given that stage, as Tuchel calls it. The head coach maintains that Pickford is his first choice, but it was Trafford he picked for both Nations League fixtures against Spain, the ones that really mattered, the ones that would strengthen or threaten his own employment.

As for Trafford's career prospects, to revisit our opening line, England's No 1 sounds like a fair vocation.

Thomas Tuchel wants England to use victory in the Nations League finals as a springboard to winning Euro 2028 at Wembley.

The head coach admits it has taken him a while to recover from the trauma of his side’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in July, for which he was heavily criticised.

But after beating world champions Spain 3-2 on Sunday night, topping their Nations League group ahead of March’s quarter-finals and next summer's finals, Tuchel is finally able to look forward with positivity and belief.

‘I saw the celebrations in Portugal when they won the Nations League,’ he said. ‘It’s just the best, the best preparation we can have for the Euros. We want to have these matches on the highest level to prove ourselves and to gain confidence, to see where we are and to adjust our game where we need to, that’s what this Nations League is perfect for. We want to win it.’

England have won five of their six matches since the World Cup, losing only to Spain at Wembley in September. In the build up to that game, Tuchel was involved in heated exchanges with observers who continued to question his tactics in the final half hour against Argentina.

’It took me a while to digest (the World Cup exit) and see the way forward, how we can help and adjust and improve, and how we can do this together,’ he said.

‘We had reviews and so on, but clarity then came together with the players. Straight away we had the energy right to take the next steps. The ideas became more clear for me, even if it was not so easy the first week, to overcome and arrive with different emotions. Some were still upset from the World Cup. Some were new in the team. Some had digested it, some had not digested it. But it was important to have this kind of process together.

‘(Spain) was a complete performance that makes me very proud. It's a full package of belief, of courage, of commitment, of togetherness, of relying on each other and stepping up in this moment.’

Tuchel, though, has rejected the idea that seeing out the win Madrid was proof that he has learned from his mistakes in Atlanta

‘Not at all, I think we would not have been in this situation if it was 11 against 11,’ he said. ‘For me, it was Mexico reloaded (not Argentina). It's one man down, but what can you do? It is their strength to have ball possession, to overload and find the gaps. It just plays totally into their hands and it comes wave after wave. It felt like three hours and thirty minutes!’

Roma, Juventus, Atalanta and Como are the four Italian clubs that are looking at the Swiss international. From England, it is Aston Villa and Nottingham Forest that are monitoring his situation closely.

#1877. Hull City vs. Brighton & Hove Albion - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 12:49, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 18:07

Brighton & Hove Albion travel to the MKM Stadium to face Hull City in Sunday's gameweek 11 contest, marking the teams' first-ever Premier League meeting.

The top flight's leading scorers occupy unfamiliar territory in second place, five points behind Arsenal, and Fabian Hurzeler's men are favourites to beat a Hull side without a victory in any competition since late August.

Had Sergej Jakirovic been offered 13th place after 10 matches before the season began, he might have accepted it, given that the Tigers had spent nine years away from top-flight football.

Indeed, the promoted outfit's manager may be relieved by his team's current position, considering that last season's Championship playoff winners have not collected maximum points in nearly three months.

An opening pair of victories over Manchester United (2-0) and Coventry City (1-0) gave supporters plenty to celebrate, before the Tigers secured a creditable third consecutive clean sheet by holding Aston Villa to a goalless draw.

Since then, Hull have exited the EFL Cup and failed to win another seven top-flight matches, extending their winless sequence to eight in the league and nine across all competitions while leaving them three points clear of the relegation places.

Jakirovic can take consolation from his team's battling qualities, which have kept all their defeats narrow: they lost 2-1 to Newcastle United, 1-0 at Fulham and 1-0 at Arsenal before the international break.

Notably, the Tigers are one of four teams yet to lose at home in 2026-27, although their seven points from an available 15 fall short of the returns collected by Arsenal (15), Brighton (13) and Leeds (nine).

Hurzeler's men will be mindful of their hosts' stubbornness in front of their supporters and overall competitiveness as the second-placed side seek to extend their unbeaten run on Sunday.

The Seagulls have won three consecutive matches without conceding, including two top-flight victories that have lifted them to second in the Premier League table.

Unlike in previous seasons, Brighton's success has been built on combining their attacking fluency with defensive solidity, highlighted by six clean sheets across their last seven league matches.

The only league fixture in that sequence without a shutout was a 2-0 defeat at Liverpool, but they have since responded by beating Manchester City 1-0 at the Etihad Stadium and overcoming Brentford 2-0 at the Amex.

Having already recorded at least three consecutive top-flight victories twice in 2026, from March to April and September to October, with the latter sequence extending to four wins, Hurzeler's men now seek to achieve the feat for a third time this calendar year.

With no side collecting more points across the last six rounds, Brighton's return of 15 from 18 matching Arsenal's, the travelling supporters will back their team to triumph in this first Premier League meeting with the Tigers.

Matt Crooks, though, is back in contention after serving a one-match suspension against Arsenal before the break for accumulating yellow cards.

#1876. Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources. After claiming the first pole of his Formula One career, an absolutely stunning effort in his 192nd attempt – edging out Mercedes’ George Russell right at the death – Alpine’s Pierre Gasly revealed that a harmless jibe from his performance coach Ben Thorpe just before the session started had riled him up.

It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.

“Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference. “There are a few of us in the paddock who are. So we have exchanged our IDs on Chess.com and we have had a little game going on.

“I won yesterday, and another one that carried on into today,” the Frenchman added. “I was feeling confident and I was picking [taking] piece after piece. Then Ben told me: ‘You are getting George here but he is going to get you in a few minutes!’. And I thought ‘F--- off!’.”

What a way to break your duck. And what a day on which to do it. On Friday, Gasly lost his only podium of the season when the International Court of Appeal reinstated two five-second penalties he received in Monaco, dropping him from third to seventh in that race. The ruling produced fireworks when Flavio Briatore, Alpine’s executive adviser, then accused one of the judges on the ICA panel of being biased towards McLaren, one of two teams who had brought the appeal.

Another 24 hours later, the fireworks were for all the right reasons. And there was no appealing the result; the start of Russell’s final lap in Q3 was slightly compromised by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, but the Englishman could have no real complaints, losing out by 0.060secs in the end, prompting wild celebrations in the Alpine garage.

To say the result was a surprise would be an understatement. This was the Enstone team’s first pole in 17 years, since Fernando Alonso took P1 Renault at the 2009 Hungarian Grand Prix.

The warning signs were there. Alpine had been quick all weekend. But the Tifosi packing Monza’s grandstands fully expected it to be a battle between Mercedes and their beloved Ferrari for pole.

The Scuderia’s performance was underwhelming. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were only ninth and 10th quickest in Q2, the latter squeaking into Q3 by one thousandth of a second from Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto. “F--- me,” Hamilton said after dodging that bullet.

And although they improved a bit in Q3, Hamilton managing to claim P5, just behind Leclerc in P4, they never threatened the front row. In fact, they later got lucky as McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, who took P3, was later hit with a three-place grid drop post-qualifying for impeding Liam Lawson, meaning both Ferrari drivers rose one place.

It could prove significant. Hamilton, like Russell, knows this weekend represents a golden opportunity to close the gap to Kimi Antonelli in the title race. The two Britons are tied second in the championship heading into the weekend, 59 points behind the Italian. But Antonelli, who sacrificed his qualifying to help Russell, must start from the back of the grid on Sunday due to exceeding the permitted number of engines in a season.

It promises to be a fascinating race, with Antonelli fighting his way through the pack and Russell and Hamilton trying to make hay while they can. Russell sounded confident. “I think they [Alpine] have got a car that’s got some good straight-line speed, which will be nice for them in the race. But, yeah, confident I’ve got the pace to go for the win.”

Could he be underestimating Gasly again? The Frenchman, who lives locally in Milan and speaks fluent Italian, has won here before. He claimed the only victory of his F1 career at Monza for AlphaTauri in 2020.

“Anything is possible tomorrow,” insisted Steve Nielsen, Alpine’s managing director. “We didn’t expect to be in pole position, we are. Tomorrow, good starts, good strategy, good pit stops – who knows? Let’s try to win it.”

Gasly himself said he had no idea what he was capable of. “My plan is to stay first as long as I can. How long is that going to be? I have no idea. My focus is going to be on my driving and making no mistakes and making the best out of what I have.” Perhaps that will be enough for another checkmate.

Antonelli acknowledged that his engine-parts grid penalty meant he had no reason not to assist his teamate Russell by offering towing assistance.

He seemed a little peeved at times on the radio, but he did his job. With Russell likely to need to return the favour for him later this season, there is no point causing bother.

He told Sky Sports: “It’s what I have to do. The team asked me and of course I did what I had to do, I tried to help as much as possible. It’s a bit weird going in two, even the lap I did alone was a bit of a weird feeling. Overall with the penalty today I had to be a good teammate and I had to help as much as I could. I think I did a good job with that and happy it worked out.”

Here’s Oscar Piastri, asked if a pole had been possible: “I don’t think so, no. I think the first lap felt good and I tried to see if anyone wanted to go in front out of the pit lane but no one did and I knew it was always going to be difficult and misjudged the braking a little bit and locked up. That was the session but good to have a decent result, it has been a while. I’ll take it.”

Alpine managing director Steve Nielsen said to Sky Sports that they were aiming high: “Pierre is a class act, as you say, if you give him the machine, he will deliver. We failed to do that a few times last year. We haven’t always given him the most competitive machinery this year, but when we have he has delivered. Particularly earlier in the season so to see the team bounce back, to see him deliver on the track he knows well, he lives locally, he lives in Milan. It was wonderful.

“We mustn’t forget Franco either, he’s done a great job today. I really feel we have given them a good car, and who knows? Anything is possible tomorrow.”

Here’s what he said immediately after the session: “Massive congrats to Pierre because that’s an incredible performance. We were actually playing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying and he beat me there and I thought ‘well I think I’ll beat you in qualifying’ and here we are - he’s ahead of me again! I was disappointed not to get pole. It was a bit messy with Verstappen opening the lap. But Pierre and Alpine have been super fast, even from Q1. Happy to see them get a good result.”

Gasly’s advantage, it appears, seems to be over Russell’s car understeering and lacking grip in turbulent air.

P1 ☝️#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/U0hebWsjWY

He says: “It was amazing, thank you everyone. It was an incredible qualy. I felt very good in the car. I was trying to chip away in evert session. I’m so happy, it’s been nine years trying to get a pole. First win [was] in Monza, to get pole is very special.”

He then pays credit to his team and the fans in Italian, and I am leaning on my Latin to get the gist of it.

“I was disappointed not to get the pole,” admits Russell who said he had been playing chess with Gasly before the game and the Frenchman won that, with Russell confident he was going to beat him in qualifying.

Alpine been in the news all weekend. Fair to say that pole lap from Gasly is better PR for the team than Flavio Briatore’s bizarre outburst in the FIA press conference yesterday. Well done that man.

His tone is evidently disappointed. In truth, given Hamilton is fifth, he is in a strong position to have the best of the weekend.

Gasly, yes, was fastest, but Russell has been the most consistent.

Piastri could be in trouble, too, for impeding earlier in the day’s sesion. Ferrari, in fourth and fifth, do not look entirely competitive.

Russell is second, Piastri third, Leclerc fourth, Hamilton fifth, Verstappen sixth, Antonelli seventh, Colapinto eighth, Norris ninth and Lindblad 10th.

He starts his flying lap, and locks up at turn 1 and exceeds track limits. That means Norris will be unable to get a tow from him too.

After being the quickest at FP2 and FP3, he is top of the pack once more with a bit over five minutes left.

Antonelli has done him a favour there, but Russell may need to return the favour in similar circumstances down the line.

Hamilton is now down in ninth, and struggling, about 0.8s off the pace.

Hamilton needs to catch Leclerc to get a tow. It failed to happen last time out.

Piastri finished Q2 in P2 but it looks likely he'll be penalised for this incident involving Lawson#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/RGzzEeqyql

Lawson, Hulkenberg, Sainz, Ocon, Bearman and Bortoleto are all out.

Hamilton is 10th, one-thousandth of a second quick enough to scrape through, and Leclrec ninth.

“**** me” exclaims Hamilton, without saying, ‘Asterisk’ once.

Antonelli asks for the chance to go out with another team ahead so he can get a tow of his own.

Norris now second quickest, so perhaps those brakes are up to speed.

There is some suggestion that Hamilton might need a front wing change.

The Silver Arrows working in tandem Kimi in front, George slipstreaming behind #F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/H476E91GJs

But Gasly is going fastest in his out lap.

Verstappen now goes fastest. Lawson is in behind, with Carlos Sainz making a surprise appearance up top.

Hamilton and Russell are yet to lay down times.

Norris is uncomfortable with his brakes at Monza.

Given he’s well outside of the fastest for now, the pressure is on him to make Q3.

The two Aston Martins are out, along with Yuki Tsunoda, Alex Albon, Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez.

Q2 awaits, with Gasly fastest - aiming for what would be his first pole.

Alonso, meanwhile, has wirthdrawn from the session. Things going wrong for the veteran, who must have no other hobbies.

FOUR MINUTES TO GO IN Q1TOP 6 ⬆️Gasly VerstappenColapintoAntonelliRussellHamiltonBOTTOM 6 ⬇️Hulkenberg AlbonBottasAlonsoStrollPerez#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BYdYjrjtnu

Pierre Gasly takes his Alpine for a spin. He is now fastest, with Verstappen second, and Colapinto bookending the Dutchman.

Antonelli and then Russell next, with the stricken Antonelli likely to give his colleague a tow.

The Red Bull man is 0.216s clear of Hamilton, with Piastri just behind.

No surprising stragglers just yet, but 11 minutes to go of this section.

We’ve 16 minutes left, and some cars are finally coming out to do battle.

18 minutes ahead before the final two rounds. Nobody is doing anything. As they say in football: tactically fascinating.

Monza paddock is absolutely sweltering. 33.8C out here. I just passed Fabio Capello on my way back to the media centre. He was speaking to Sky Sports Italia so I wasn’t able to give him my thoughts on where he went wrong at the 2010 World Cup.

Decent ding dong between Hamilton and Verstappen in practice earlier. Hopefully Hamilton is fired up for this. With Antonelli taking his grid drop at his home race, there’s a big opportunity for both Hamilton and Russell to close the gap this weekend.

The tifosi are ready 🙌It's time for qualifying at the Temple of Speed 👊#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/jeiTcb8Ij2

The cars will soon be out on the track, and we’ll have reports of their progress.

There are actually times when affection for a car company makes sense, despite what I said earlier.

Sound on... listen to the reception for Charles and Lewis ❤️#F1 #ItalianGP @ScuderiaFerrari pic.twitter.com/kk6BvA1UdC

As touched on earlier, Lewis Hamilton has to hope Charles Leclerc will work with him.

The Monegasque (look it up) is the junior partner at this point, whether he wants to be or not. That might not make him entirely delighted, but he can tow the British driver around and give him a launch for fast laps, if he’s feeling helpful.

Everyone now has access to PowerPoint, which means we all now have to have, “learnings.”

Imagine if someone you met in real life said that to you.

3 hours of laps and learnings done.#ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/GTvOvL5L5M

Given Antonelli is still one of the quickest on the track, it would be no surprise if he can at least make the top 10.

Favourable accidents and yellow flags might offer up more opportunities, too, but both Hamilton and Russell need to strike while they have such a clear advantage.

George Russell tops Lewis Hamilton in final practice in Monza 🇮🇹💪 pic.twitter.com/jxIO13aRX6

I’m as big a fan of F1 as the next man, assuming the next man quite likes F1, but there is something strange about supporting a car company, isn’t there?

🇮🇹 Sentendo il calore dell'Italia! 🥰🇬🇧 Feeling the warmth of Italy! 🥰 pic.twitter.com/ze6Ww1Z0zx

The session starts in around 40 minutes, so drivers are on their Gameboys and Instagram, and reading the weekend edition of The Telegraph.

Words we live by, this weekend and always ❤️ pic.twitter.com/0QoGlpzOHI

Here’s our interview with Alex Albon about a grim weekend at Monza.

“Alex Albon remembers the 2022 Italian Grand Prix well. He had been looking forward to it. ‘We had a car which was good down the straights that year so I was quite excited to be going to Monza,” the Williams driver recalls, a little wistfully.

‘We did FP1 and FP2 and sure enough we were quick so I was like: ‘This is going to be a good weekend.’

“Albon could not have been more wrong. He remembers waking at around 1am that night and being unable to get back to sleep.

“What happened next was the stuff of nightmares. Albon called the doctor, was diagnosed with appendicitis, sent to San Gerardo Hospital in Monza for surgery, only to suffer an unexpected complication during the procedure, which resulted in acute respiratory failure.”

He shares the joint record with Michael Schumacher for most wins at Monza.

Schumacher, a Ferrari legend, ended his career with five. Hamilton has the same.

Sport loves an emotional link to records, so be prepared for this to become a big moment.

Five wins apiece for Michael and Lewis 🖐#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/j10lMygYft

The Italian team are bringing an upgrade engine to Monza for the weekend.

Hamilton would desperately love to go out at the top after what is a remarkable return to decent form after some years of desperate struggle.

With Antonelli possibly out of the running this weekend, this is the chance to change the - *spits in self-scorn* - narrative.

Russell might have incurred a penalty if he had done this in qualifying.

The Mercedes man blocked Oscar Piastri’s run at a corner, forcing some heavy braking from his rival.

Thankfully, Piastri ducked out, and thankfully for Russell, he’s not facing censure.

A near miss for Oscar Piastri! 😬 pic.twitter.com/y6UMu8wIDM

Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton go racing! 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Zs8u8h4XoT

The former world champion is still looking for more from his car.

“Just looking at the deltas there, I was losing something like 0.6secs to George on the straights, which is something we need to look into,” Hamilton said yesterday, before explaining his conundrum for qualifying, suggesting he may go out after Leclerc.

“The tow is everything here so [I’m] likely to be looking for the tow.”

Because Antonelli exceeded the limit of parts used for his engine, he is taking a grid penalty at Monza.

Few would entirely rule out a storming ride for him on Sunday to end up top of the pack, but is is clearly a huge task for him to score points of any kind with that disadvantage.

They are now likely both past their peaks, but Hamilton and Verstappen recalled their battles of 2021 when they clashed in practice earlier.

Verstappen was already hacked off with Hamilton for seemingly obstructing his path earlier in the session, and they almost came together in the dying moments of the session.

Hamilton needed to take the escape road at the first chicane, where the pair made contact in 2021, as Verstappen looked to slip around his occasional rival. The two of them scarcely avoided another contact.

On the radios, Verstappen claimed, “He caused that,” while Hamilton reported to Ferrari that he was, “Blocked by Max.” Perhaps there will be more aggro later.

The full list of times from earlier today.

FP3 CLASSIFICATIONRussell in the box seat heading into qualifying#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BUrCsv92dT

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

#1875. Thomas Tuchel is now embracing traditional English values - clarity has helped England understand who they are, and now they can beat the best, writes CRAIG HOPE

Published: 16:57 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 16:57 EST, 16 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel has always liked what he sees from his England players on the training pitch. Less so, at times, inside a stadium. It is a contradiction with which he has wrestled since the World Cup, when performances on the whole left him underwhelmed, save for the collective spirit and individual excellence that rescued results.

It is why, when the squad reconvened at St George’s Park in September, Tuchel used the meeting room as much as he did the grass to address that disparity in delivery.

At the same time, the elephant in the corner of the auditorium was the German’s own comments about the DNA of English players compared to the likes of Spain, and fundamentally them lacking the coding to protect possession and, therefore, valuable leads. He asked Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and others for their thoughts.

The message back from his players was this – let us be better at being us, not them. Interestingly, that was Tuchel’s mantra upon his appointment, one of embracing traditional English values. Amid the World Cup fallout, though, he had wandered in a daze down a rabbit hole of genetics, focusing on what his team cannot do as opposed to what they can.

Tuchel, his staff and his players are tacticians and technicians, not scientists. If the intricacies of DNA do not allow them to be Spain, then don’t be. Be England, they determined. That is not to say kick and rush, bark and bite. After all, Kane is officially the best player in the world right now and Bellingham, unofficially, is playing as well as anyone on the planet.

Rather, there needed to be clarity – this is what we are and this is how we beat the best. On Sunday night in Madrid, England beat the very best. It was a victory born from those hours on the training field and in conference, and even more spent by Tuchel and his assistant Anthony Barry during their post-tournament review in a St George’s Park war room. They knew then that this was not a case of rip it up and start again, more so mend the tears and give the likes of Bellingham a blank sheet to impact where, and how, he sees best.

Thomas Tuchel is embracing England's DNA and reaping the rewards following the World Cup

England can now beat the best, which they showed against Spain in a fantastic victory

There was no radical strategical change, but there was a new doctrine, principles that should underpin whatever the in-game circumstance – off-the-ball running, a high press, filling in for a team-mate who has seized a moment to improvise elsewhere, such as the full backs. Ben White scoring England’s third on Sunday and Lewis Hall completing four more dribbles than Lamine Yamal were examples of Tuchel’s allowance for greater intuition. Be you, not Spain.

Kane, informally at least, has also been promoted beyond captain, a bridge between management and dressing-room. To see him in a semi-coaching and cajoling capacity on the touchline after he was taken off in the 78th minute against Spain was to witness this elevation.

But even if England had conceded a late equaliser at the Metropolitano Stadium, it would not have mattered. Not when it comes to measuring post World Cup improvement. To have drawn comparison with Argentina and that second-half collapse would have been unfair and inaccurate. The semi-final was 11 versus 11 and so let us judge this game on the same terms. And what did England do with a 1-0 lead and 11 players? They attacked. And attacked again. For all of the tweaks Tuchel and Barry have made to the structure of training and the team’s set-up, this was evidence of them learning from a mistake, as much as the head coach will be loath to admit.

Ezri Konsa, however, did reveal there was a definite instruction to keep attacking Spain when Tuchel addressed the team at half-time.

‘The instruction was to keep going at them,’ said the defender. ‘Don’t stop. To keep our foot on the pedal. That is what we did. Argentina was different, different circumstances. But it was not just half-time. We went 1-0 up and Harry, our captain, told us to keep going and to keep our foot on the pedal too.'

Before Jarell Quansah’s needless mistake and Elliot Anderson’s subsequent dismissal in the 63rd minute, the game was not in the balance in any way. As a live observer of almost every Tuchel match since his arrival, this was the best performance of his reign. In fact, it’s not even close.

And yet, so much still comes back to Bellingham. England would not have won without him. He terrified Spain, perhaps given their intimate knowledge of his powers. Beating the best is as much a mental challenge as it is physical, and Bellingham believed. He made England believe, too. His swagger. His majesty. And yes, his skill. He won the corner for Konsa’s headed second and created the third for White. He then dropped into midfield when down to ten and battled and organised like a captain.

Bellingham has bought into the collective under Tuchel and, with that, his team-mates are buying into his big ideas. For now, they don’t come much bigger than what England achieved in Madrid.

#1874. More than just a football club: Cardinale’s vision to make AC Milan a multi-billion empire

In case you weren’t aware from his repeatedly bold comments in the media, Gerry Cardinale has big plans for AC Milan.

The RedBird Capital founder and chief has made one concept very clear: while he is at the helm, Milan are no longer just a football club, but a platform that aims to integrate sports, infrastructure, and entertainment. Of course AC Milan will be at the centre of the web, but the idea is to expand.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The proof of this comes from a three-letter acronym: MSE. It stands for Milan Sports & Entertainment and it is the new holding company created by RedBird. The idea, simply put, is to bring together investments and activities in various sectors under one umbrella.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport recall, Cardinale explained to the Financial Times that the assets involved could be valued in the mid-single-digit billions, meaning several billion dollars. So, how does he plan to get there?

Cardinale linked the creation of MSE to the process initiated with the acquisition of Milan: “Milan Sports & Entertainment is the culmination of this work and of what we have built since we first invested in the club four years ago.”

In his interview with La Gazzetta, Cardinale clarified that the new structure is also created to support the Rossoneri’s sporting ambitions: “The driving force behind operations like this is to provide Milan with the financial strength needed to compete in the transfer market and secure the best players in the world.”

There are examples of this kind of model working already. Kroenke Sports & Entertainment, AEG and Fenway Sports Group are among the most prominent and – given his background in the USA – Cardinale knows each of them well.

According to CNBC valuations, KSE was worth $26.05bn in 2026, FSG $15.37bn, and AEG $11.99bn in 2025, excluding music and hotel businesses.

KSE boasts franchises such as the Los Angeles Rams, Denver Nuggets, Colorado Avalanche and Arsenal, as well as venues such as SoFi Stadium, Ball Arena, and Emirates Stadium. The group combines sports, infrastructure and real estate development such as Hollywood Park, the district built around SoFi Stadium.

AEG – founded by Philip Anschutz – have instead built its model on the management and development of venues. It owns or manages venues such as Crypto.com Arena and The O2 in London plus the Los Angeles Kings and LA Galaxy, and operates in concert promotion and ticketing. The LA LIVE project developed around Crypto.com Arena puts the venue at the centre of a greater ecosystem.

Fenway Sports Group – born around the Boston Red Sox and Liverpool FC – have developed a holding company with interests in media, marketing, real estate, and entertainment. It’s a model Cardinale knows first hand: in 2021, RedBird invested approximately $750m in FSG, acquiring a stake of around 11%, based on an enterprise valuation of $7.35bn.

MSE in theory can harness elements of all three of these experiences: KSE’s integration of sports and infrastructure, AEG ‘s commercial development of facilities and FSG ‘s multi-sport approach. The main difference is the purpose declared by Cardinale: to use all of it to funnel money back into Milan.

From the stadium shared with Inter to the possibility of an arena in San Donato, including the new NBA Europe venture and even tennis: MSE’s scope includes various initiatives that go beyond the playing field.

The main infrastructure project is the future Generali Stadium, the new 71,500-seat facility designed by Foster + Partners and Manica. Developed jointly by the two Milanese clubs, it represents a key element of the transformation of the San Siro area and will not be a Rossoneri-only facility.

The promoters intend for the stadium to host year-round activities, from matches to concerts, as well as catering, events, and hospitality services. In other words, like the stadiums and arenas mentioned above, it will become more than just a place to go for two hours on a Sunday.

In San Donato Milanese, RedBird are also considering the possibility of building a 20,000-seat arena. Cardinale explained that the fund already owns the land and has planning permission, but the idea is also linked to Milan’s potential involvement in NBA Europe. Another area of ​​focus concerns tennis, with the possibility of hosting a tournament in the city.

Finally, RedBird intend to develop a company dedicated to managing stadiums and arenas, with services including catering, merchandising and premium hospitality. The goal is to build commercial expertise to apply to the facilities connected to the group, but also to make it available to other owners and sports clubs.

This phase will be co-ordinated by Brett Yormark, appointed CEO of MSE and set to step down as head of the Big 12 (a conference in College Football) at the end of January 2027. He worked for 14 years at Brooklyn Sports & Entertainment, overseeing the development of the Brooklyn Nets and the Barclays Center. He has also gained experience in NASCAR and Roc Nation.

The choice to go for Yormark reflects the desire to entrust the platform to someone with expertise across multiple different fields in the sporting and commercial worlds.

All these grand plans are well and good, but how will ideas turn into money that drives AC Milan forward? MSE’s economic potential is measured not only through the club’s revenues, but also through the activities that RedBird intends to develop around sports, infrastructure and entertainment.

The starting point is obviously Milan as a club, which closed the 2025-26 financial year with revenues of €464.6m, over €100m of which came from sponsorships. The main infrastructure opportunity is the new San Siro, an investment of approximately €2.3bn shared with Inter.

Projections contained in the design documents indicate a potential annual revenue of approximately €120.4m for the facility as a whole (both for the Rossoneri and the Nerazzurri), through sporting, commercial, and complementary services

These are numbers that will be revised upwards by the two clubs when considering, for example, the record agreement with Generali for naming rights. It is worth a total of €650m over 25 years, divided into €10m per year for the first five years and €30m per season for the following 20, once the stadium is built.

One of the areas on which RedBird Capital are focusing most is hospitality, which is currently worth around €15m per year for the Rossoneri. The international benchmark has already been set by Legends Global, a company Cardinale knows well.

Legends are what the Milan owner sees as a model for developing premium services, restaurants, and commercial spaces. The most obvious example is at FC Barcelona: with the support of LG, the club have marketed nearly 5,000 VIP seats at Camp Nou, generating over €380m in contracted revenue.

They aim to generate another €700m through multi-year licenses for an additional 2,000 seats. This isn’t annual revenue, but rather contracts spread over 15 or 30 years, so a guaranteed flow of money coming in that Cardinale aims to replicate.

Another agreement which demonstrates the potential of this kind of arrangement is the one with Real Madrid for the Santiago Bernabéu. It involves an investment of approximately €360m in exchange for 20-year participation in some of the stadium’s businesses,.

Legends Global also operate in facilities and events management. Following the acquisition of ASM Global (who actually proposed renovating San Siro for non-football events in Italy) in 2024, the group claims a presence in over 450 venues, approximately 20,000 events, and 165 million guests annually. Their European partnerships include Arsenal, Chelsea and Porto.

FC Barcelona launches new VIP seating licenses at Spotify Camp Nou with Legends Global

🔗 More details: https://t.co/awtEsnYE6X pic.twitter.com/iCMuM0QD35

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) September 25, 2026

To illustrate the potential it could hold for Italy as a whole, the English subsidiary reported revenues of £131.6m in 2024, of which £105.5m came from facility and event management and £26.1m from catering. Before the integration with ASM Global, Legends had reported revenues of $1.7bn in the period ending in March 2024, with 67% coming from food and beverage sales.

In Italy, a benchmark is Forumnet, who in 2024 generated €29.7m in revenue and €12.8m in EBITDA (Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation). They manage the Assago Forum which hosts approximately 60-70 concerts a year, demonstrating how a venue can generate activity well beyond the sports calendar.

As mentioned, an arena is being planned in San Donato with an estimated investment of around €400m, which could become the basis for a Milanese franchise in NBA Europe. For reference, Olimpia Milano – the current basketball team in the city – generate around €15m through ticketing, season tickets, sponsorships and merchandising.

For NBA Europe, projections speak of over $1.5bn to be distributed to the clubs in the first six years. A theoretical division among the 12 permanent franchises would equate to approximately $20.8m per team per year, but this is not fixed yet. Entry costs – estimated by the media to be between $500m and over $1bn – also remain to be determined.

Tennis represents another potential area for development. The ATP 500 in Halle generates around €5m in revenue, excluding television rights, while the ATP Finals in Turin generate around €60m. These are events with different dimensions and scopes, but they provide a scale.

The creation of MSE has a stated objective: to strengthen Milan’s financial capacity and reduce the gap with the richest clubs on the international scene, particularly those in the Premier League.

The gap is also evident when comparing revenues. AC Milan closed the 2025-26 season with €464.6m, a significant result considering their absence from European competitions , but still far from the top English clubs.

According to the Deloitte Football Money League, in the 2024-25 season, Liverpool generated €836.1m, Arsenal €821.7m and Manchester United €793.1m. Tottenham and Chelsea also exceeded €670m and €580m, respectively.

The comparison covers different financial years, but it still shows the magnitude of the gap. Liverpool generated revenues equal to approximately 1.8 times those of Milan, while Chelsea recorded a turnover approximately €120 higher.

The chasm shows how clubs in the Premier League have showcased an ability to generate commercial revenue, enhance stadiums and reach a global audience. The gap has only been growing, and TV rights will be another focus, though that is outside of just Cardinale’s hands.

Speaking of the owner, it is now obvious he sees MSE as the name that will house the tools to try build a real sporting and commercial world around Milan. It remains to be seen how effective it will be, but the starting point is there.

#1873. Getafe vs Atletico Madrid - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 13:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 13:03

Atletico Madrid will be aiming to avoid a third straight defeat in all competitions when they continue their La Liga campaign against Getafe on Sunday.

This is a fixture that has been played on 47 occasions throughout history, with Atletico comfortably leading the overall head-to-head record 32 victories to Getafe's five.

Getafe have been beaten in five of their last six matches against Atletico, but they do have a recent home win to their name over the Red and Whites, triumphing 2-1 in March 2025.

The Deep Blue Ones have a record of three wins, three draws and six defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 12 points leaving them in 15th spot in the La Liga table.

Jose Bordalas' side entered the November international break off the back of a 2-0 defeat to Villarreal, while they were also beaten 1-0 by Brighton & Hove Albion in the Conference League in their last home fixture on November 5.

Getafe have the joint-worst attacking record in Spain's top flight this season, having only managed to find the back of the net on eight occasions in 12 matches.

The Deep Blue Ones are only two points outside of the relegation zone, but they have been impressive on home soil this season, boasting a record of three wins and three draws from their six league fixtures in front of their own supporters.

Atletico, meanwhile, sit third in the La Liga table, boasting a record of nine wins, one draw and two defeats from their 12 matches to collect 28 points.

Diego Simeone's side are two points behind second-placed Real Madrid and five points off the leaders Barcelona, who beat the Red and Whites 2-1 before the November international break.

Atletico also lost to Bayern Munich in the Champions League on November 3, so they will be bidding to avoid a third straight loss in all competitions in this fixture.

The Red and Whites have been impressive on their travels in Spain's top flight this season, picking up 15 points from their six league games on the road.

Atletico will be bidding to record their 10th league victory of the season on Sunday before welcoming Viking to Madrid in their next Champions League match on November 25.

Getafe will be without the services of Nemenja Gudelj, who is suspended after picking up a milestone yellow card in the clash with Villarreal last time out.

Christiantus Uche, Zaid Romero and Juanmi will also miss out through injury.

Enes Unal is the capital outfit's leading goalscorer this season with four, and there should be another start in the final third of the field for the 29-year-old.

As for Atletico, Alejandro Grimaldo needs to be assessed due to a recent illness, while Marc Pubill is a doubt due to an injury that he sustained on international duty with Spain.

Ademola Lookman and Cristian Romero are also expected to miss out this weekend.

Morten Hjulmand could return in the middle of the Atletico midfield, while Julian Alvarez is likely to be joined in the final third of the field by Lee Kang-in.

Soria; Carvajal, Boselli, Djene, Mojica; Garcia, Terrats, Mangala, Martin; Unal, Satriano

#1872. England left sweating as Harry Kane faces months out with ankle injury

England captain Harry Kane is facing three months out with an ankle injury, Bayern Munich have confirmed.

The Ballon d’Or winner scored against both Croatia and Spain during the recent international break and was seeking a first goal in five matches for the Bundesliga leaders against Cologne at the Allianz Arena on Friday night.

However, as he looked to latch on to Michael Olise’s deflected low cross at the back post, Cologne full-back Joel Schmied got to the ball first and clattered into Kane’s left leg during his follow-through.

Kane immediately clutched his lower leg and writhed in pain for a few moments before gingerly getting back to his feet, but he was a virtual bystander for the next couple of minutes.

The 33-year-old gestured to the dugout, sunk to the turf and then received treatment on his ankle before making way for Tom Bischof, limping off the field alongside two physios.

Kane had a quick exchange with Bayern boss Vincent Kompany, back in the dugout for the first time in six matches after being diagnosed with meningeal irritation last month, before heading down the tunnel.

Speaking at full-time, Kompany confirmed that Kane was facing months on the sidelines with what Bayern director of sport Max Eberl described as a tear of the syndesmotic ligament.

Sky Germany has reported that he can expect to spend three months on the sidelines, meaning he will hope to return before England face Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in March.

An official Bayern statement read: “Harry Kane sustained a syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle during this evening’s home match against 1. FC Köln. This was confirmed by an examination carried out by FC Bayern’s medical department. The 33 year-old will be sidelined for the next few months. Get well soon, Harry!”

Matters only grew worse for Bayern thereafter, as Olise was also forced off shortly after Kane with a foot injury. He was able to walk off the pitch before treatment and has been diagnosed with a bruised forefoot that should only keep him on the sidelines for a matter of days.

Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore opened the scoring for Cologne after just 12 minutes on Friday night, but the match finished 1-1 as Nathaniel Brown equalised for Bayern before the break.
